title: On the Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
hook: On-policy distillation isn't a midpoint between fine-tuning and RL — it carves its own narrow path through parameter space, locking into a low-dimensional subspace early in training.
key_points: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own generations, scored by a teacher — but its training dynamics were poorly understood.
In parameter space, OPD sits in a 'relaxed off-principal regime': it changes fewer weights than SFT, yet stays less tightly constrained than RL with verifiable rewards.
'Subspace locking': OPD's cumulative updates rapidly collapse into a narrow, low-dimensional channel — and that early subspace alone is enough to preserve its performance.
Mixing in verifiable-reward RL changes the geometry; going off-policy or sparsifying update tokens does not.
content_html: On-policy distillation (OPD) — where a student generates its own tokens and a teacher scores them — is increasingly used to sharpen LLM reasoning, but its training dynamics were poorly understood. This paper maps where OPD actually moves a model's weights and compares it against supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR).
extra_html:
What they found

Using a suite of parameter-space diagnostics, the authors place OPD in a "relaxed off-principal regime": compared with SFT, its updates touch fewer weights and avoid the principal directions more strongly; compared with RLVR, they stay less tightly constrained. Beyond that static picture, OPD shows subspace locking — its cumulative updates quickly enter a narrow, low-dimensional channel. Restricting training to the subspace formed early on preserves OPD's performance but badly degrades SFT, suggesting that locked subspace is functionally sufficient for OPD specifically.

Why it matters

Control experiments sharpen the story: sparsifying the update tokens or shifting generation off-policy preserves the rank dynamics, while mixing OPD with RLVR changes them. The takeaway is that OPD is not merely an interpolation between SFT and RL — it induces its own update geometry. That reframes how we think about cheap post-training: the method you choose shapes where in parameter space learning happens, not just how well the model ends up doing.

related.title: Trust Region On-Policy Distillation
related.hook: On-policy distillation breaks when teacher and student disagree too much. TrOPD only trusts the teacher where its supervision is reliable — and skips the rest.

related.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
related.hook: A big model's softened probabilities say more than hard labels - they reveal how classes relate, so training a small model to mimic them transfers knowledge a one-hot target never could.

related.title: GRPO: Group Relative Policy Optimization
related.hook: GRPO dropped the value network from PPO and scored each answer against a group of sampled siblings — the cheap RL recipe that made DeepSeek-R1's reasoning trainable.

related.title: OPID: On-Policy Skill Distillation for Agentic RL
related.hook: Outcome-only RL tells an agent it failed but not which move was the mistake. OPID mines that lesson from the agent's own finished trajectories — turning hindsight into dense, per-token supervision.
